problems.heading: What Tsumugi solves
problems.lead: Using Cloudflare Queues directly as a job queue causes several problems.

items.title: Job state is hard to track, and succeeded jobs are not kept
items.queues: Queues provides no API to query the state of an enqueued message.
items.tsumugi: The Tsumugi dashboard and REST API list, search, and aggregate both running and finished jobs.

items.title: Mutual exclusion and deduplication are hard to implement
items.queues: Queues does not manage dependencies or relationships between messages.
items.tsumugi: In Tsumugi, jobs with the same `concurrencyKey` run one at a time, in order.

items.title: More job types mean more branching
items.queues: Queues allows only one consumer per queue.
items.tsumugi: Tsumugi distinguishes job types by binding name, which is the export name of the performer, so the consumer needs no branching.

items.title: Messages are occasionally lost
items.queues: Queues provides no way to detect messages that were lost without being processed.
items.tsumugi: Tsumugi marks a job as unresponsive when a job that has started does not report its result.

code.heading: The code you write
code.lead: You write code in only two places: the job handler and the enqueue call.
steps: Define the job handler as a performer

compose.title: Built from performers and enqueue
compose.body: You define the job handler as a performer and call enqueue where you submit the job. Tsumugi handles delivery, execution, and state tracking.

builtinCard.title: Job management built in
builtinCard.body: Retries, backoff, delayed jobs, scheduled jobs, priority, concurrency and rate limits, deduplication, and a dashboard are standard features of Tsumugi.

history.title: Finished jobs stay visible
history.body: The dashboard and REST API list and search every job, including succeeded and failed ones. With the `TSUMUGI_METRICS` binding configured, Tsumugi also records failure rate and duration metrics.

flow.title: Workflows with dependencies
flow.body: Declare nodes and their dependencies, and each node's return value is passed to the next node as its payload. With fan-out, a child node is created for each element of an array and runs in parallel.

async.title: Asynchronous work with a method call
async.body: Calling `enqueue(env, {'{'} binding, payload {'}'})` enqueues a job. The call returns the job ID and completes immediately.

guarantee.title: Per-job execution guarantees
guarantee.body: A job with `guarantee` set to `at-most-once` never runs twice. The default `guarantee` is `at-least-once`.

remote.title: Performers in another Worker
remote.body: Tsumugi runs performers even when they live in another Worker connected through a Service Binding.
